limits: Source implementation and available regression completion are distinct from Windows build/runtime verification. Windows dcc64/bcc64/CNG/Schannel/SDK/D3D11 and CI runner were not executed.
All A/B/O must be rebuilt and newly approved together; ImGui ABI2 must not be mixed with old object/DCU files. Explicit legacy cohorts remain compatible; mixed Handoff generations are rejected.
Reauthentication and mandatory manifest/CI checks retain their previous OFF defaults until explicitly configured. Trusted proxy and HTTPS deployment require real environment settings.
The provided Windows pipeline requires an interactive protected self-hosted runner and independently managed approval/CI keys; no remote CI installation or operating deployment was performed.
CI evidence authenticates a trusted signer claim, not hardware attestation. Portable CI tests use synthetic PE/outcome inputs and do not fabricate Windows PASS evidence.
Single-writer coordination is for a local SQLite-capable filesystem and upgraded writers; no HA/shared-filesystem fencing or whole-disk rollback guarantee.
Audit outbox repairs unacknowledged process-crash operations. Later deletion of already acknowledged audit files or entire storage rollback is not automatically repaired.
Server close is best effort when disconnected; server expiry limits remaining authority. Audit/history are retained and local file deletion remains subject to OS locks.

Call gates require owners to stop publishing references before Free; they do not make a dangling pointer safe. Process-owned API modules and a bounded readonly arena intentionally survive until OS teardown.
Owned temporary plaintext buffers are shortened/wiped; managed RTL, provider, allocator and OS copies cannot be guaranteed absent.
Independent software CNG keys and authenticated IPC do not provide TPM attestation or protection from a fully compromised local administrator/kernel.
Hash measurement rules are unchanged. Separate RSA-OAEP/signature/TLS/key-ID SHA-256 uses are not obsolete file/code hash paths.
No new debugger/security-tool suppression or foreign-process injection was added. ImGui is upstream C++ statically linked through a Delphi C ABI; Injection remains an unconfigured UI action.
Only the requested first five improvement categories are covered. The next categories remain deferred until user build feedback.
